faq.q: What is the cheapest hen party boat in Marbella?
faq.a: Our Tier A boats – the Astondoa 40 (12.5m, 9 pax) and Azimut 39 (12.5m, 11 pax) – are the most budget-friendly. At €749 for 2 hours or €2,299 for 8 hours, they include skipper, fuel, drinks, snacks, insurance, and VAT. Perfect for a small group wanting a taste of luxury without overspending.

faq.q: How much should I budget per person for a hen party boat in Marbella?
faq.a: For a group of 10 on an Azimut 39, an 8-hour charter costs €2,299 – that's €230 per person. Add food, decorations, and maybe a photographer, and you're looking at €300–€350 per person. For a premium experience on a Mangusta 80 (12 pax), the 4-hour minimum is €4,719, so about €393 per person.

faq.q: What's included in the hen party boat price?
faq.a: Every charter includes a licensed skipper, fuel, water, soft drinks, beer, white wine, cava, light snacks, insurance, safety equipment, and Spanish IVA (21%). So the price you see is the price you pay – no surprises. You can bring your own decorations and a cake, but check with us about any restrictions.

faq.q: Can we bring our own food and drinks on board?
faq.a: Yes, you're welcome to bring your own food and additional drinks. We provide a starter pack of drinks and snacks, but many hen parties bring a birthday cake, tapas, or a picnic. Just let us know in advance so we can ensure there's enough fridge space.

faq.q: What is the best time of day for a hen party boat in Marbella?
faq.a: For a summer hen party, a 4-hour morning slot (11:00–15:00) is great for swimming and sunbathing. For sunset vibes, choose a 2-hour evening charter (18:00–20:00) to see the coast glow. An 8-hour full-day charter gives you the best of both – lunch, swimming, and a golden-hour return.

faq.q: Do we need to pay a deposit to book a hen party boat?
faq.a: Yes, a 30% deposit secures your date, with the balance due 7 days before departure. We accept bank transfer or card. For last-minute bookings (within 7 days), full payment is required. Cancellations up to 14 days before get a full refund – after that, the deposit is non-refundable.

faq.q: Can we hire a photographer or DJ on the boat?
faq.a: We can arrange a professional photographer (approx. €150/hour) or a DJ (approx. €200/hour) for your hen party. These are add-ons and must be booked in advance. Alternatively, many groups bring their own Bluetooth speaker – our boats have sound systems you can connect to.

faq.q: What happens if it rains on our hen party day?
faq.a: Marbella averages 320 sunny days a year, so rain is rare. If the captain deems conditions unsafe, we'll reschedule at no extra cost. If you choose to cancel, you'll receive a full refund. We'll always suggest a better date if the forecast looks poor.

data.body_html:
Planning a hen party in Marbella and want to know exactly what it'll cost? Here's a transparent 2041 budget breakdown for a marbella hen party boat – no hidden fees, just honest numbers. Whether you're after a budget-friendly afternoon on an Astondoa 40 or a full-on luxury bash on a Mangusta 80, this guide covers prices, inclusions, and tips to stretch your euros further.

Why a boat is the ultimate hen party venue

Forget crowded bars and overpriced VIP tables. A private boat in Puerto Banús gives you the freedom to swim in crystal-clear coves, sunbathe on deck, and party with your own playlist – all while the skipper handles navigation. You'll see Marbella's coastline from the best angle: the sea. With capacities from 5 to 12 guests, there's a boat for every bridal party size.

Our 2041 pricing tiers – what you'll actually pay

We keep pricing simple. Here are the two main tiers for hen party charters:

All prices include the licensed skipper, fuel, water, soft drinks, beer, white wine, cava, light snacks, insurance, safety equipment, and Spanish IVA (21%). So the quote you get is the final price.

Budget breakdown for a typical 8-hour hen party

Let's assume a group of 10 on an Azimut 39 (11 pax) for a full day (8 hours). Here's how the costs stack up:

  • Boat charter (8h): €2,299
  • Food/platters (optional, from local caterer): €150–€250
  • Decorations (balloons, banners): €50–€100
  • Photographer (optional, 2h): €300
  • Total: €2,799–€2,949
  • Per person (10 guests): €280–€295

If you skip the photographer and bring your own food, you can keep it under €250 per person. For a shorter 2-hour sunset cruise on the same boat, it's just €75 per person – a bargain for a special memory.

How to save money on your hen party boat

Three tips to keep costs down:

  • Book on a weekday – our weekday rates are the same as weekend, but availability is better, and you can sometimes negotiate a later start.
  • Choose a 4-hour charter – you get enough time to swim, eat, and cruise without paying for a full 8 hours. Many groups find 4h is perfect.
  • Bring your own food and extra drinks – we provide the basics, but you can bring a birthday cake, tapas, or a bottle of your favourite spirits (subject to responsible consumption).

What about the premium option: Mangusta 80?

If you're celebrating in serious style, the Mangusta 80 (24m, 12 pax) is a showstopper. At €4,719 for a 4-hour minimum, it's a splurge – but it includes a free jet ski, which is a huge hit with hen parties. That's roughly €393 per person for 12 guests. You get a massive sundeck, a flybridge, and the kind of presence that turns heads in Puerto Banús. For a truly unforgettable day, it's worth the premium.

Planning your itinerary: where to go

From Puerto Banús, you can head east to the sandy beaches of Cabopino or west towards Estepona and Sotogrande. Popular hen party stops include:

  • Cala del Faro – a quiet cove for swimming
  • Cala Cortés – crystal-clear waters near Cabopino
  • Marbella Marina – for a photo op with the yachts
  • La Concha mountain backdrop – perfect for sunset photos

Your skipper knows the best spots based on the weather and your preferences. Just tell them you want a mix of swimming, sunbathing, and partying.

Booking process and what to expect

Booking is simple: contact us via WhatsApp for availability, pay a 30% deposit to secure your date, and the balance is due 7 days before. On the day, arrive at Puerto Banús 15 minutes early – we'll handle the rest. The boat is fully equipped with safety gear, and the skipper is licensed and experienced. You can bring your own decorations, but please avoid confetti cannons that could harm marine life.
